B.title: General usability
B.intro: Please rate GlucoCompanion on the scales below. Tap the point that best matches your impression. Each scale has 7 steps between the two terms.

C.title: App consolidation
C.intro: Many people with diabetes use several apps in parallel — sensor app, logbook, insulin tracker, nutrition app. How do you rate GlucoCompanion in this context?

D.title: Gluco
D.intro: Gluco is an AI-supported chatbot you can talk to about daily life with diabetes. Please rate the following statements.

E.title: Mood & insights
E.intro: GlucoCompanion links your glucose readings with mood entries and provides insights. You can also enter free text that the AI converts into structured data.

F.title: Trust & privacy
F.intro: A few final questions about trust and data protection.

H.title: Open questions
H.intro: Finally, we would like to hear your own words. Your answers help us most to improve the app.

items.a2: What type of diabetes do you have?
items.a3: How many years have you had diabetes?
items.a4: What is your main form of therapy?
items.a5: How many digital diabetes tools (apps, sensor apps, logbooks) do you use regularly?
items.c9: GlucoCompanion could replace or complement several of my current diabetes apps.
items.c10: A single app for glucose tracking, logbook, and emotional exchange would noticeably simplify my daily diabetes routine.
items.c11: If GlucoCompanion could also show sensor data (e.g. FreeStyle Libre, Dexcom), the app would be useful for me in everyday life.
items.d12: Gluco responded empathetically to my concerns.
items.d13: I could imagine talking to Gluco about frustrations or worries related to my diabetes.
items.d14: The Buddy clearly keeps the role of an emotional companion and does not give medical dosing recommendations.
items.d15: It was clear to me that the Buddy's answers come from AI and may not be error-free.
items.d16: An empathetic AI companion like Gluco would be a useful addition to existing diabetes apps.
items.e17: The mood–glucose correlation made a new connection visible to me.
items.e18: The AI interpretations in Insights are understandable and plausible.
items.e19: The app encourages me to pay more attention to my mood in connection with my diabetes.
items.e20: Features for emotional self-management like GlucoCompanion offers are missing from the diabetes apps I have used so far.
items.e21: AI-supported free-text entry in the logbook (e.g. "Lunch: pasta, 60g carbs") makes documentation much easier for me.
items.f22: It is clear to me which of my data are stored in the app and which are not.
items.f23: I trust how my data are handled in this app.
items.f24: The information on privacy and AI is written in an understandable way.
items.g25: I could imagine continuing to use GlucoCompanion beyond the study if the app were available.
items.g26: I would recommend GlucoCompanion to other people with diabetes.
items.h27: What did you like most about GlucoCompanion?
items.h28: What bothered you about the app, or what did you miss?
items.h29: If you could change or add one feature — which would it be?
